Trump Isn’t as Powerful as He Seems
After more than a decade of Trump looming over American politics, many believe that he can do whatever he wants, says the columnist Jamelle Bouie on “The Opinions.” But he urges us to remember: Just because there’s a will doesn’t always mean there’s a way.
- I think that there is a tendency to treat the desire and will of the president as equivalent to ability and capacity. And so they say we want to do these things. And they say, and they make these threats. And I think that there’s a tendency, because of all the crazy stuff we’ve experienced over the last 10 years, to say, well, if they say they really want to do it, then it must be a thing that they can do. And I just, my view has always been: Is it though? Thinking both practically and thinking politically. Thinking about the interplay of forces and institutions and people, like, they may try, but that doesn’t mean they’re going to succeed. That doesn’t mean people should be complacent. But I do think it means that one should try to ... I’m going to do a me thing. So in his memoirs, Ulysses S. Grant tells this really interesting story. During the Mexican war. And he is out with a writing partner and they hear wolves, and Grant’s like, we’re surrounded by wolves. What are we going to do about this? And his writing partner was like, let’s just go check out and see what this is. And they go find the wolves and there’s only two wolves. And Grant’s like, there’s always more of them before you count them. That’s where we are. There’s always more of them before you count them. – OK. – Being able to have a clear view of what the landscape looks like, I don’t think, again, shouldn’t make you complacent, but should give you a better sense of what are the actual possibilities here. And how can we deal with those?
